title: Cities: Skylines | Power, Politics, & Planning: Episode 3: Gentrification
premise: Donoteat01 argues new housing and downzoning fail incumbent renters in different ways, advocating incremental decommodification while acknowledging economic risks.
coverage: 52nd Street faces redevelopment, rising rents, and displacement. Mock property ads and oversized rent-control cards accompany competing housing policies and a qualified argument for decommodification. Policy claims are the presenter's account.

panels.description: Blue Chirper mascot above curved terrain beneath episode 3 GENTRIFICATION and series title.
panels.camera: The aerial opening transitions to the title card, then fades to black.

panels.heading: The game neighborhood visibly unhappy
panels.description: Many red frowning-face unhappiness icons float above row houses surrounding a cleared paved vacant lot beside the freeway. A red-frown location pin marks the lot; ordinary traffic and green-white streetcars remain visible.
panels.camera: An oblique gameplay view catches the brief burst of red unhappiness icons.
panels.action: Unhappiness indicators appear above nearby properties after the lot is cleared.
panels.visualGag: A chorus of unhappy game faces accompanies the claim that construction directly displaces residents, reversing the opening everyone-wins premise. Deliberate comic staging is uncertain.

panels.action: Book overlay on gameplay then disappears.
panels.visualGag: Retitled Mao tract visually introduces combatting gentrification; setup for later rejecting Maoist shortcuts.

panels.heading: Comrade objection
panels.description: WELL, ANYTHING'S POSSIBLE AFTER THE REVOLUTION, RIGHT COMRADE? caption over gameplay.
panels.camera: Overhead and oblique editor views change angle and distance.

sound.text: March of the Volunteers, the Chinese national anthem, accompanies the comrade caption, Mao mass-killings article and Chinese flag. The patriotic music satirizes the revolutionary shortcut that the narrator rejects.

panels.visualGag: Satirical objection made visible; connected setup for following Maoist article rebuttal.

panels.heading: Maoist rebuttal
panels.description: A Wikipedia-style article titled Mass killings of landlords under Mao Zedong appears, followed by a Chinese flag overlay.
panels.visualGag: March of the Volunteers accompanies the mass-killings article and Chinese flag, turning the comrade objection into a dark satirical shortcut. The narrator explicitly rejects mass killings.

panels.heading: Jeremy Corbyn in the train cab
panels.description: A large photograph of Jeremy Corbyn in an orange high-visibility vest and navy cap, seated at a train-cab control desk, overlays gameplay. Another hi-vis wearer stands behind him; game margins remain visible. It accompanies the reference to his proposed worker purchase rights.
panels.camera: Cut to the static train-cab photograph, then back to gameplay.
panels.action: Corbyn sits with a hand near the train-cab controls; another hi-vis wearer stands behind him.
panels.notes: The train-cab portrait gives his worker-purchase proposal a mildly playful illustration.

panels.heading: Worker purchase as an analogy for tenant finance
panels.description: Gameplay returns to low-rise houses and a newly placed building beside an internal parking area. The presenter carries Corbyn's worker-co-op proposal into a proposed financing-bank analogy for tenants.
panels.camera: Cut back from Corbyn to changing oblique gameplay views of the block.
panels.action: Construction previews and cursor detailing continue as the presenter develops the financing analogy.
